summary: Survey + adversarially verify every viable way to run ONE callback on the UE GameThread from an injected thread in a stripped Shipping build
logs: GT-01: surveying five GameThread-dispatch mechanism families against UE 5.4.4 source
survey complete: 5 families analyzed, 2 anchor reports
0 of 5 family best-candidates survived adversarial review

synthesis.recommended_mechanism: One-shot swap of a single Blueprint UFunction's 8-byte `UFunction::Func` field, reflection-addressed (never by RVA), on a live GameThread-ticking BP UFunction — with OUR own `extern "C"` trampoline (three plain pointers, identical ABI profile to the proven ESC-01 ProcessEvent call) as the replacement. The trampoline runs synchronously on the GameThread when the engine dispatches that UFunction, restores `Func` as its first act, records thread identity into an injector-owned page, then forwards to the original `&UObject::ProcessInternal`. This is the ONLY family that simultaneously: (a) runs OUR code on the GameThread — which is what lets the callback record its own thread identity (the owner's PROVE requirement) and, in phase 2, issue the reflection-located LoadAsset_Blocking call; (b) crosses the MinGW->MSVC boundary with plain pointers only, no TFunction/FString/TDelegate construction; (c) is genuinely one-shot and self-restoring with nothing persistent left behind; (d) needs zero raw engine addresses. Primary target: a BP class UFunction confirmed-live-and-ticking via a fresh read-only ERI pass; a viewport-resident `UUserWidget` BP `Tick` override is the alternate (Slate ticks it every frame with no bCanEverTick/replication gate). NOTE: this recommendation is CONDITIONAL on two read-only pre-flight gates passing (Func offset measurement + live ticking-target confirmation); if either fails, GT-01 is BLOCKED, not answered by a fallback.
synthesis.why_narrowest: Mutation footprint is 8 bytes at one offset inside ONE UObject on the process heap. No code page is written (no VirtualProtect on .text, no FlushInstructionCache, no mid-write-execution race), no .rdata page is made writable, no engine container is touched, no UObject is created or registered. The hook exists for at most one dispatch — the trampoline restores `Func` before it does anything else — so its lifetime is a fraction of one frame for a per-frame target, versus a persistent hook. Only our own code executes; the payload (phase 1) writes nothing but POD into a page we own. The ABI exposure is exactly the plain-pointer C-ABI vtable-slot pattern already proven safe in ESC-01, not the TFunction/FString construction that is fatal in families 1, 3 and 4. It self-restores with nothing to uninstall, and — decisively — it is the same mechanism that carries phase 2, so GT-01 needs to validate ONE mechanism, not two. Compared with the only viable alternatives: vtable-slot-77 (ProcessEvent) patching mutates a class-wide shared .rdata vtable process-wide; any code detour needs a code address we have refused to derive (LOG-0071) and touches every caller in the process.
rejected_with_reasons: FTSTicker::GetCoreTicker().AddTicker — semantically ideal (lock-free TMpscQueue enqueue, native one-shot via return false, GameThread drain at LaunchEngineLoop.cpp:6161). Addresses ARE rigorously derivable in this image (adversaries proved it: caller-side InName literals 'RetirePakReaders'/'FBackgroundableTicker'/'InterchangeManagerTickHandle' each single-LEA into R8, converging on GetCoreTicker=RVA 0xf53370 and AddTicker=RVA 0xf4ded0). REJECTED regardless because (a) both AddTicker overloads take a TFunction/FTickerDelegate BY VALUE — an MSVC TFunction_OwnedObject with a per-lambda RIP-relative vtable that MinGW g++ cannot construct; (b) the callback AND its destructor run on the GameThread at an unknown later frame (Ticker.h:40, Ticker.cpp:131) with no completion signal, an async use-after-unload against the proven FreeLibrary recipe; (c) worst case is a silent permanent engine-wide wedge of the core ticker if the injected producer stalls between the two MpscQueue publish stores.

AsyncTask(GameThread, TUniqueFunction<void()>) and FFunctionGraphTask::CreateAndDispatchWhenReady — thread-safe dispatch and exactly-once, but the parameter is TUniqueFunction<void()> BY VALUE (Async.h:449, TaskGraphInterfaces.h:1760), an MSVC-constructed non-POD MinGW cannot build; AsyncTask has no anchor and CreateAndDispatchWhenReady is a fully-inlined header-only static with no out-of-line symbol.

UEngine::DeferredCommands / console / CVar sinks — REJECTED at the family level: DeferredCommands carries an engine exec STRING and executes ZERO of our code, so it structurally cannot satisfy 'execute one callback' or provide any thread-identity proof channel; NO_LOGGING/stripped strings give no observable; the append races the GameThread's own RemoveAt(0,N) which by default ResizeShrinks and frees the buffer (steady state is Data=null/Num=0/Max=0, so no slack ever); CVar sinks/OnBeginFrame are non-thread-safe TArray/TDelegate registrations that are persistent hooks with a dangling-call-after-FreeLibrary failure; ProcessUserConsoleInput runs on the calling thread; setting a CVar off-GameThread is silently broken in Shipping (check(0) compiled out).

Reflection-only 'schedule not do' routes incl. PrimeSoundForPlayback — REJECTED: the only memory-safe delegate targets are ZERO-parameter UFunctions (ParmsSize==0 makes ProcessEvent's memcpy a no-op), and a zero-parm callee can take/return/capture nothing, so it has NO channel to record thread identity — it cannot meet the owner's PROVE requirement even in principle. Additionally PrimeSoundForPlayback: CreateSoundWaveProxy + AddOrTouchChunk take a process-global cache lock across unbounded blocking disk IO (can stall the GameThread), TrimMemory can free 10% of the cache and release retained audio on live assets, at least three mutually indistinguishable silent-no-op paths make a null result uninterpretable, and the target's NumChunks>1 precondition and a nonzero FUObjectItem::SerialNumber are both non-reflectable prerequisites.

GGameThreadId read as an oracle — plain uint32 global (CoreGlobals.cpp:428) but zero-init => lives in ~3.5MB BSS tail of .data with no string/export/reloc/RTTI anchor; any dynamic scan is circular (the search key is the TID we are trying to prove). In Shipping it is not even the engine's decision variable — IsInGameThread() reduces to the thread_local ActiveTaskTag.

Calling IsInGameThread()/reading ActiveTaskTag/FThreadManager::GetThreadName from the callback — no symbol/export/string/RTTI to locate; ActiveTaskTag needs an unrecoverable TLS index/offset; GetThreadName returns an FString across the ABI boundary.
vtable-slot-77 patch or any .text detour — larger blast radius (class-wide shared vtable, or every caller in the process) and a code address we have no verified derivation for (LOG-0071).

steps: PHASE 0 — read-only pre-flight (ERI class, NtQueryInformationThread + ReadProcessMemory only; no writes, no injection). 0a. Snapshot all threads (CreateToolhelp32Snapshot/THREADENTRY32); for each OpenThread(THREAD_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION)+GetThreadDescription. REQUIRE exactly one thread named L"GameThread" => TID_E1 (else ABORT). 0b. Independently: earliest-created thread by GetThreadTimes/GetProcessTimes, and NtQueryInformationThread(ThreadQuerySetWin32StartAddress) == liveModuleBase + AddressOfEntryPoint(RVA 0x5CADA90 from the PE header) => TID_E2. REQUIRE TID_E1==TID_E2. 0c. For that TID, NtQueryInformationThread(ThreadBasicInformation)->TebBase; RPM TEB+0x08 StackBase, TEB+0x1478 DeallocationStack, TEB+0x48 ClientId.UniqueThread==TID_E1. Persist {TID_GT, TebBase, DeallocationStack, StackBase}.

PHASE 0 (cont.) — MEASURE the UFunction::Func offset; do NOT assume 0xD8. Offline, from the UHT static FNameNativePtrPair arrays (Anchor Report 1, Tier 2) build name->predicted-exec-thunk-RVA for a few hundred native UFunctions across several classes (e.g. KismetSystemLibrary exec thunk for LoadAsset_Blocking = RVA 0x37445f0). Live, for each such UFunction found by name via the GUObjectArray walk, sweep candidate offsets 0xB8..0x120 in 8-byte steps and record which single offset reproduces the static prediction for ~100% of natives while every other offset matches ~0%. Accept the offset ONLY on that unanimity. As a by-product: read Func on thousands of non-native BP UFunctions and confirm one identical shared value == &UObject::ProcessInternal (Class.cpp:6940). This pins Func AND cross-validates the static table from two derivations sharing no intermediate. If no clean offset emerges => BLOCKED, stop.

PHASE 0 (cont.) — choose the target and confirm it live, read-only. Fresh ERI GUObjectArray pass: find a UBlueprintGeneratedClass UFunction that (i) is named ReceiveTick or Tick, (ii) has FunctionFlags@(measured 0xB0) with FUNC_Native(0x400) CLEAR, (iii) has UStruct::Script ArrayNum@0x68 > 0 (so ProcessEvent does not early-return at ScriptCore.cpp:2015), (iv) has EventGraphFunction@(measured 0xC8) == nullptr (so the fast-call at ScriptCore.cpp:2044 cannot bypass us — ReceiveTick is immune anyway, it has a float parm), (v) whose owning class has LIVE instances in GUObjectArray and whose native ancestor chain reaches AActor::Tick (or, for a widget, UUserWidget in the viewport). Candidate BP_MasterHoldable_C::ReceiveTick is live-verified (CR-01) but its tick is conditional (OnRep_TickEnabled) — prefer a target confirmed actually ticking, or a viewport-resident UUserWidget BP Tick (no bCanEverTick gate). Record Orig = qword at UF+Func_offset; REQUIRE Orig == the shared ProcessInternal value AND Orig on a .pdata RUNTIME_FUNCTION start (corroboration only; never called by us).

PHASE 1 — build the record page and trampoline. Injector VirtualAllocEx a single RW page in the target (injector-owned, so the READ-ONLY instrument renders the verdict and the page survives DLL residency). POD layout, naturally aligned: magic, hitCount, tid(I1 sentinel 0xFFFFFFFF), injectorTid, rsp(I3), retAddr0(I4), qpc, and a separate N1 self-test slot {selfTid, selfRsp, selfRet}. The trampoline is extern "C" void Tramp(void* Context, void* Stack, void* Result): ~15 instructions, no allocation, no engine call, no C++ object.

PHASE 2 — negative control BEFORE arming. N1: call the identical recorder synchronously on the injected CreateRemoteThread thread into the self-test slot. Pre-register: it MUST yield selfTid != TID_GT, selfRsp OUTSIDE [DeallocationStack, StackBase) of TID_GT, and selfRet NOT inside MISERY .text [0x1000,0x5DCAA9C). If the recorder cannot tell our own thread from the GameThread, the instrument is invalid => ABORT.

PHASE 3 — arm (the ONLY write, 8 bytes). Publish Orig and &Tramp into DLL statics with release ordering. Immediately re-read and REQUIRE UF->ClassPrivate == the live 'Function' meta-class, UF->NamePrivate == expected FName, UF->OuterPrivate == expected BPGC. Then InterlockedCompareExchangePointer(&UF->Func, &Tramp, Orig). If the CAS observes anything other than Orig => the field changed under us => abort, write nothing further.

PHASE 4 — the trampoline (on the GameThread, synchronous, in this exact order). T1 InterlockedIncrement(hitCount). T2 InterlockedCompareExchangePointer(&UF->Func, Orig, &Tramp) — RESTORE FIRST, tolerate failure; the hook is now gone. T3 if InterlockedCompareExchange(Fired,1,0)!=0 { call Orig(Context,Stack,Result); return; } — a concurrent/stale entrant forwards without consuming. T4 record GetCurrentThreadId()->tid(I1), RSP via asm(movq %rsp)->rsp(I3), __builtin_return_address(0)->retAddr0(I4) (level 0 ONLY; its immediate caller is UFunction::Invoke at Class.cpp:6847, i.e. engine .text), QueryPerformanceCounter. T5 payload = ONLY those POD stores (phase 1: no allocation, no UE call, no package load). T6 call Orig(Context,Stack,Result) — forward so the BP tick still runs.

PHASE 5 — disarm/timeout and read the verdict. Wait for Fired or a bounded timeout (a few seconds is generous for a per-frame target). On timeout with hitCount==0: under a VEH guard, re-validate ClassPrivate/NamePrivate/OuterPrivate read-only, then InterlockedCompareExchangePointer(&UF->Func, Orig, &Tramp) (unique &Tramp is a strong anti-ABA token; if the CAS fails the trampoline already restored). NEVER FreeLibrary. The read-only instrument then reads the page once and applies the pre-registered agreement rule.
addresses_and_how_derived: Target UFunction object address — reflection, GUObjectArray walk BY NAME (ERI I-04/I-05, proven). Not an RVA.

UFunction::Func byte offset — MEASURED read-only by the population test above, cross-checked against the offline UHT FNameNativePtrPair static table; accepted only on ~100%/~0% unanimity. Not the inferred 0xD8 on faith.
EventGraphFunction (+~0xC8), FunctionFlags (+0xB0), Script ArrayNum (+0x68) — proven/measured anchors from the same pass (0xB0 live-confirmed 247/247 by ERI I-05).

Original Func value (== &UObject::ProcessInternal) — READ out of the field, never interpreted; corroborated by mass agreement across thousands of BP UFunctions and by landing on a .pdata function start.
Trampoline address — inside our own MinGW DLL, known at runtime.
ProcessEvent — UObject vtable slot 77, already proven (ESC-01). No new RVA.

External GameThread TID — GetThreadDescription==L"GameThread" (E1) and initial-thread/Win32StartAddress==ImageBase+0x5CADA90 (E2). NEED NO address inside the target image at all (E1) / only a PE header field (E2).
TEB fingerprint (TebBase, StackBase, DeallocationStack) — NtQueryInformationThread + RPM. No image address.

PHASE 2 payload only: /Script/Engine.KismetSystemLibrary:MakeSoftObjectPath, :LoadAsset_Blocking, /Script/Engine.Default__KismetSystemLibrary — all by name via reflection (present at script-objects.tsv:11836 / :11821 / :8299).
gt01_design.exactly_once_guard: Two layers. (1) The trampoline's FIRST real act (T2) is InterlockedCompareExchangePointer restoring Func, so the hook lives for at most one dispatch, not one frame. (2) An InterlockedCompareExchange(Fired,1,0) gate (T3) elects exactly one payload runner; any concurrent or stale-register entrant (a thread that loaded &Tramp before the restore landed) tail-forwards to Orig and is merely counted in hitCount for evidence. The payload therefore executes exactly once even if the trampoline is ENTERED more than once, and the entry count is measured rather than assumed. For an actor tick, the N same-class instances dispatch serially on the GameThread within a frame (bRunOnAnyThread false), so concurrency is not expected; the gate is belt-and-suspenders because we cannot prove from outside that no parallel path exists.
gt01_design.restore_and_rollback: Func is restored inside the trampoline (T2) before any payload, via a CAS whose compare value is our unique &Tramp — a 64-bit anti-ABA token a reused allocation would essentially never hold at that offset. If the callback never fires, the disarm path re-validates the object read-only under a VEH guard and CASes Func back; if that CAS fails, the trampoline already restored. The only mutated engine state is 8 bytes at UF->Func, returned to the exact value read pre-flight. The record page is injector-owned VirtualAllocEx memory (never freed during the run; a permanent-until-process-exit reservation is the accepted cost). NEVER FreeLibrary: a thread can hold &Tramp in a register across our restore, so unmapping the trampoline would be a use-after-unmap crash on the GameThread — this is a deliberate departure from the ESC-01 flow and must be written into the probe. No .text, .rdata, vtable, or engine container is mutated, so there is nothing else to roll back.
gt01_design.abi_notes: The trampoline is extern "C" void Tramp(void* Context, void* Stack, void* Result): three pointer-sized args in RCX/RDX/R8 under MS x64, void return, no FP args, no aggregate by value. mingw-w64 emits ms_abi by default (write __attribute__((ms_abi)) explicitly as documentation). FFrame& is a plain pointer; RESULT_DECL is void* const. We construct/copy/destroy NO C++ object — no FString/TArray/TFunction/TDelegate/TSharedPtr/FFrame, no temporaries — exactly the plain-pointer profile of the proven ProcessEvent call, categorically unlike the disqualified TFunction-by-value families. Build with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti, no global ctors, small frame (avoid __chkstk_ms); verify the built DLL actually emits .pdata/.xdata so an engine stack-walk through our frame does not fault. Use __builtin_return_address(0) ONLY — level 1 walks the RBP chain and MSVC /O2 engine callers are frame-pointer-omitted, so level 1 is an access-violation primitive. Keep the trampoline free of any thread_local/emutls touch: the GameThread predates our DLL load, DLL_THREAD_ATTACH never ran for it, so a TLS access could lock/allocate on the GameThread. PHASE 2 note: LoadAsset_Blocking takes TSoftObjectPtr<UObject> BY VALUE, whose only non-POD member is FString SubPathString — provably a valid empty FString as zeroed memory (null-guarded dtor, Len()==0), and empty by construction for a path with no ':' delimiter. The FNames are minted by the engine via MakeSoftObjectPath from a UTF-16 buffer WE own: ProcessEvent memcpys our POD Parms in, the thunk deep-copies, and on return memcpys the frame copy back over our buffer rather than freeing it — so the engine never calls FMemory::Free on MinGW memory. Every non-POD value is either all-zero bytes or written into our buffer by MSVC engine code.

proof_oracle.method_1: EXTERNAL identity, established read-only BEFORE the callback exists: GetThreadDescription over all threads yields exactly one L"GameThread" => TID_E1 (LaunchEngineLoop.cpp:2278 + WindowsPlatformProcess.cpp:2327/2445; the OS thread so named is definitionally the one whose id fed GGameThreadId). Independently, the process initial thread (earliest creation time AND Win32StartAddress == liveModuleBase+0x5CADA90) => TID_E2 (Launch.cpp:92 FTaskTagScope(EGameThread) wraps the whole tick loop; Win64 => game thread == initial thread). REQUIRE TID_E1 == TID_E2. Fingerprint that TID with E3 (TebBase, StackBase, DeallocationStack).
proof_oracle.method_2: INTERNAL provenance, recorded by the trampoline and genuinely independent of method_1: (a) GetCurrentThreadId() == TID_E1; and (b) __builtin_return_address(0) minus liveModuleBase falls inside MISERY .text [0x1000,0x5DCAA9C) and resolves offline (chain-following .pdata lookup) to UFunction::Invoke — proving the callback was invoked BY engine dispatch, not by our own thread. (b) is not a restatement of (a): a fabricated TID could satisfy (a) while (b) fails, and our-own-thread execution fails (b) even with a matching stack. Also check DeallocationStack <= RSP < StackBase (StackLimit is NOT used — the kernel lowers it as the stack grows).
proof_oracle.negative_control: N1: the identical recorder is called synchronously on the injected CreateRemoteThread thread, into a separate slot, BEFORE arming. Pre-registered requirement: selfTid != TID_E1, selfRsp OUTSIDE [DeallocationStack, StackBase) of the GameThread, selfRet NOT inside MISERY .text. If the recorder cannot distinguish our own thread from the GameThread, every later reading is worthless and the whole experiment aborts. N2: after arming nothing, re-read the page and confirm hitCount==0 / tid==sentinel (proves the record is written only by dispatch).
preregistered_outcomes: hitCount==1 AND tid==TID_E1==TID_E2 AND retAddr0 in .text (resolves to Invoke) AND DeallocationStack<=rsp<StackBase AND N1 distinguished AND a re-run of E1/E2 after the fire is unchanged => PASS: the callback executed exactly once on the Unreal GameThread. GT-01 confirmed; phase 2 authorized.

hitCount==0 at timeout => callback NEVER fired. Restore Func anyway (VEH-guarded). Meaning: target was not actually ticking, OR the measured Func offset was wrong, OR arming failed. NOT a refutation of the mechanism by itself; re-open target selection / offset measurement. BLOCKS phase 2.

hitCount>1 => trampoline ENTERED more than once. The Fired gate still bounds the PAYLOAD to one execution, so if tid is consistent across the single recorded slot the run is still informative, but flag it and investigate the dispatch multiplicity before phase 2.

tid != TID_E1 (or != TID_E2) => fired on the WRONG thread, i.e. the chosen UFunction was dispatched off the GameThread (unexpected for an actor/widget tick). FAIL. Do NOT proceed to phase 2; the mechanism's GameThread assumption for that target is false.
retAddr0 NOT in MISERY .text => the callback was invoked by non-engine code or by our own thread (e.g. our thunk page). FAIL — provenance not established.
N1 fails to distinguish (selfTid==TID_E1, or selfRet in engine .text) => the instrument itself cannot separate threads. ABORT the entire experiment; no positive result is trustworthy.

failure_modes: Callback never fires (hitCount==0 at timeout): target not ticking (BP_MasterHoldable tick is OnRep_TickEnabled-conditional), or measured Func offset wrong, or the arming CAS never observed Orig. Handling: bounded timeout -> VEH-guarded restore CAS regardless -> report FAIL. Meaning: target-selection or offset error, NOT necessarily a mechanism refutation. This is the silent-timeout trap the project warns about; it is distinguished from a genuine mechanism failure by the pre-flight gates (offset measured, ticking confirmed) having passed.

Fires more than once (hitCount>1): concurrent or stale-register entrant. The InterlockedCompareExchange(Fired,1,0) gate keeps the PAYLOAD exactly-once; extra entries forward to Orig and are counted as evidence, not executed. Investigate dispatch multiplicity before trusting the run for phase 2.

Fires on the wrong thread (tid != TID_E1==TID_E2): the UFunction was dispatched off the GameThread. Caught by method_2. FAIL, do not proceed. Would mean the target's tick path is not GameThread-serial as assumed (e.g. an AnimBP-reachable path) — pick a different target.
Called by our own code, not the engine (retAddr0 not in .text): provenance failure caught by method_2 + N1. FAIL.

Func offset wrong / measurement ambiguous: caught pre-flight (no ~100%/~0% unanimity, or +0xC8 EventGraphFunction degeneracy). BLOCKED before any write; never arm on an ambiguous offset. Writing 8 bytes to the wrong offset (e.g. +0xC8) does not create a hook but redirects ProcessEvent into the fast-call branch — which is exactly why the offset is measured, not assumed.

GC destroys the target UFunction during the arm window (level unload, class purge): mitigated by a sub-frame window, identity re-validation (ClassPrivate/NamePrivate/OuterPrivate) immediately before arm and before the timeout restore, and the unique-&Tramp anti-ABA CAS. The disarm restore runs under a VEH guard so a freed/unmapped page faults into the guard rather than crashing. Not fully closable from source — a stated residual.

DLL unloaded while a thread holds &Tramp: prevented by NEVER calling FreeLibrary. The trampoline code stays resident for the process lifetime (accepted leak). A late second entrant into an unmapped trampoline would be a GameThread AV — the never-unload rule is what removes that.
Integrity check over UObject heap flips Func back or detects the write: unknown (no evidence either way); the sub-frame window and immediate self-restore minimize exposure. Residual.

Phase-2-specific: FSoftObjectPath resolves to NAME_None (names not interned) -> LoadSynchronous silently returns null. Prevented by MakeSoftObjectPath minting the names first and asserting PackageName.ComparisonIndex != 0 before the LoadAsset_Blocking call. Also assert SubPathString bytes are zero after MakeSoftObjectPath (no engine allocation left in our buffer).

result.critique:
I verified the load-bearing source claims against the on-disk UE 5.4 tree before critiquing. Findings below.

---

## What I checked and found SOUND (not vague praise — specific verifications)

- **The dispatch anchor is correct.** For a ProcessEvent-dispatched BP event, `UObject::ProcessEvent` calls `Function->Invoke(this, NewStack, ReturnValueAddress)` (ScriptCore.cpp:2141), and `UFunction::Invoke` executes `return (*Func)(Obj, Stack, RESULT_PARAM);` (Class.cpp:6836/6847). So `UFunction::Func` IS the swap point, and `__builtin_return_address(0)` from the trampoline genuinely lands in `UFunction::Invoke`. Method_2(b)'s provenance claim is source-accurate. (Note: there are *other* `(*Func)` sites — execCallMathFunction ScriptCore.cpp:1075, the EX_CallMath opcode path — but the ProcessEvent/tick route is unambiguously through Invoke. Verified they don't collide.)
- **`Func == &UObject::ProcessInternal` for BP functions is real** (Class.cpp:6940), so the "Orig == shared value across thousands of BP UFunctions" acceptance check is grounded, not hopeful.
- **E1 is sound.** `FWindowsPlatformProcess::SetupGameThread()` → `SetThreadName(TEXT("GameThread"))` (WindowsPlatformProcess.cpp:2329), and `SetThreadName` calls the real `SetThreadDescription` (2445-2451), which is what `GetThreadDescription` reads back. The game thread is queryably named. Good.
- **The `Script.Num()==0` early-return gate (ScriptCore.cpp:2015) and the EventGraphFunction fast-call (2041-2049) are exactly where the design says.** Its diligence on those two branches is real.

---

## Prioritized gaps

### G1 — Entire mechanism families were never considered; the "narrowest" claim is undefended against them. (highest priority)
The rejected list is thorough *within* the five families it enumerates, but three or four families are simply absent, and at least two are plausibly **narrower** than the recommended 8-byte heap write:

- **Hardware-breakpoint (debug register) + VEH, gated on the GameThread TID.** Set `Dr0` = ProcessEvent's address — which is *already a verified code address* from ESC-01 (slot 77 was called successfully, so it is not a LOG-0071 unverified RVA) — via `SetThreadContext` on **only** the GameThread (debug registers are per-thread, so only that thread traps). Install a VEH that gates on `GetCurrentThreadId()==TID_E1`, records POD, clears `Dr0` (one-shot), returns `EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_EXECUTION`. This writes **zero** bytes to engine memory — narrower than 8 bytes on the "engine mutation footprint" axis the design uses to argue narrowest. Never mentioned.
- **`SuspendThread` + `SetThreadContext` RIP redirect.** Redirect the GameThread's RIP to our own stub (save context, run POD payload, restore). Zero engine bytes written, no code address needed at all, inherently one-shot, and proving GameThread execution is trivial (you picked the thread). For **phase-1 GT-01 specifically** (POD-only, no loading) this is dramatically narrower and *skips the entire unmeasured-Func-offset gate that can BLOCK the whole design*.
- **Per-instance vtable clone / vptr swap.** Clone one live object's vtable, redirect slot 77, repoint that object's vptr. Touches one object (8-byte vptr write at offset 0 — no offset measurement needed), not the class-wide shared vtable the design correctly rejected. Dodges the Func-offset uncertainty entirely.
- **`QueueUserAPC`** deserves at least a one-line rejection (the GameThread almost never enters an alertable wait in a tight loop → the APC starves → the same silent-timeout trap). Its absence is a completeness hole.

**What closes it:** add these four to `rejected_with_reasons`. The honest rejection of the debug-register and context-hijack families is *phase-2 reentrancy* (see G3), not footprint or ABI — and that reason only applies to phase 2, which means for phase-1 GT-01 they are arguably the correct, narrower choice. That reframes the whole "one mechanism for both phases" decision (G2).

### G2 — Phase-1/phase-2 coupling is a choice presented as a necessity, and it inflates phase-1 risk.
The design couples GT-01's proof to the phase-2 delivery mechanism ("validate ONE mechanism, not two"). But phase 1 is explicitly a *separate, earlier* step with a non-loading callback. Forcing phase 1 to adopt phase-2's constraints (a known-safe dispatch point, a measured Func offset, a confirmed-ticking BP target) imports phase-2 risk into a proof that could otherwise be done with a zero-engine-write context hijack (G1). **What closes it:** state the coupling as a deliberate trade-off, and consider proving GT-01 with the simplest mechanism first, then separately validating the Func-swap as the phase-2 carrier.

### G3 — The recommended mechanism runs phase-2's blocking load at a NESTED, mid-script-VM re-entrancy point, and this hazard is not in the failure-mode list.
The trampoline fires *inside* `UFunction::Invoke` *inside* `ProcessEvent` *inside* the BP tick's own `ProcessEvent`. Phase-2's `LoadAsset_Blocking` → `FlushAsyncLoading` therefore runs re-entrantly nested in the script VM. In Shipping the reentrancy `check()`s are compiled out (`DO_CHECK==0`), so a bad nesting corrupts **silently**. This is precisely the safety advantage the *rejected* Ticker family had — it drains at a clean point between systems, not mid-VM. The design trades the Ticker's ABI hazard for a reentrancy hazard and discusses only the ABI side. **What closes it:** add nested-reentrancy to `failure_modes`; argue from source (or concede) that `FlushAsyncLoading` nested inside a tick `ProcessEvent` is safe in this build; note the visible multi-ms GameThread hitch.

### G4 — The proof oracle's "two INDEPENDENT methods" is overstated; method_2(a) reuses method_1's value.
Method_2(a) is `GetCurrentThreadId() == TID_E1` — a direct comparison against method_1's output, not an independent derivation. The RSP-range check also derives from method_1's TEB fingerprint (E3). The *only* genuinely independent internal signal is method_2(b): `retAddr0 → UFunction::Invoke` (engine-dispatched vs. our-own-thread). **What closes it:** reframe honestly as "one externally-established identity (doubly-derived via E1==E2) + one independent *provenance* fact (invoked by engine dispatch)." These prove two *different propositions* ("which OS thread" and "invoked by engine"), which is genuinely valuable — but they are not two independent measurements of the same fact, and "which thread is the GameThread" has exactly one source of truth (the external naming). Do not sell it as more.

### G5 — Phase 2 silently expands scope beyond the ONE call the owner authorized.
The owner authorized "ONE call of `LoadAsset_Blocking`." The design adds a **second** GameThread-executed engine call, `MakeSoftObjectPath`, as a prerequisite (to intern the FNames). That is a real, defensible engineering need — but it is an unauthorized additional callback and must go back to the owner as an explicit re-scope, not be folded in. **What closes it:** surface it; get sign-off for exactly two named reflection calls, or find a single-call path.

### G6 — The Func-offset population test's primary leg leans on an unverified static table — the ESC-02 defect pattern.
Leg 1 (matching live `Func` values to statically-predicted native exec-thunk RVAs like `0x37445f0`) is only as good as the UHT `FNameNativePtrPair` extraction, which is *asserted* ("Anchor Report 1"), not shown here. If that parse is subtly wrong the "unanimity" can still land on a wrong offset if errors correlate. **Leg 2** — thousands of BP UFunctions sharing one identical `Func` value that also sits on a `.pdata` function start — is independent of the static table and is the trustworthy leg. **What closes it:** make leg 2 the *primary* acceptance criterion, demote leg 1 to corroboration, and BLOCK if the two legs disagree. Do not accept the offset on leg-1 unanimity alone.

### G7 — The EventGraphFunction gate rests on a FALSE rationale, but source shows the gate is probably trivially satisfied in the cooked build — for a reason the design never states.
The design says "ReceiveTick is immune anyway, it has a float parm." That is **wrong**: the fast-call validates `ParmsSize == sizeof(EventGraphParams)` where `EventGraphParams` is an `int32` = 4 bytes, and a float `DeltaSeconds` is also 4 bytes — a float parm does not make it immune. The real protection is `EventGraphFunction==null`. And here is the substantive finding: the **only** runtime writer of `->EventGraphFunction` is BlueprintGeneratedClass.cpp:475, inside `#if UE_BLUEPRINT_EVENTGRAPH_FASTCALLS` **and** inside `WITH_EDITORONLY_DATA` (patched from `FastCallPairs_DEPRECATED`, comment: "can't bump engine version to serialize it directly"). `UE_BLUEPRINT_EVENTGRAPH_FASTCALLS` defaults to 1 (Build.h:365), but the *populating* code is editor-only. Strong implication: **in the cooked Shipping target, `EventGraphFunction` is null for all BP functions, the fast-call branch at ScriptCore.cpp:2044 is never taken, and ReceiveTick Func-swap is viable.** This *helps* the design — but it means the design hedged toward a widget out of a concern that likely doesn't apply, on a rationale that is factually wrong. **What closes it:** drop the float-parm claim; confirm live that the target's `EventGraphFunction==null` (expected, per source); and note this inverts the widget-vs-actor preference.

### G8 — Internal contradiction: "nothing persistent left behind" is false as written.
`why_narrowest` says the mechanism "self-restores with nothing persistent left behind," while `restore_and_rollback` and the residuals commit to a **permanent resident DLL** (never `FreeLibrary`) and a **permanent `VirtualAllocEx` page**. The *hook* is not persistent; those two artifacts are (until process exit). **What closes it:** fix the wording to "no persistent hook / no persistent engine-memory mutation," and confirm the owner's "no persistent hook" constraint tolerates a permanent resident module per run.

### G9 — Operational gap: how does the read-only instrument find the record page?
The injector `VirtualAllocEx`s a page at a randomized address; the read-only ERI instrument must read it to render the verdict, but the address hand-off is unspecified. **What closes it:** specify an out-of-band manifest (injector writes the page base + layout to a run-manifest file the instrument reads).

### G10 — E2's entry-point assumption is a single point of silent failure not gated as one.
E2 requires the initial thread's `Win32StartAddress == base + AddressOfEntryPoint`. If anti-cheat/DRM starts the process **suspended** or shims the entry (residual acknowledges the possibility), E2 breaks and the E1==E2 cross-check silently degrades to E1 alone — losing half the external-identity proof without flagging it. **What closes it:** make E2's derivation a hard pre-flight gate that, on failure, explicitly downgrades the confidence claim rather than quietly proceeding on E1.

---

## On the questions posed directly

- **Is the negative control real?** Yes, but weak. N1 can only fail if the recorder is broken; a correct recorder passes trivially. The experiment as a whole *can* genuinely fail (hitCount==0 timeout, tid≠TID_E1, retAddr not in .text are all real non-pass branches), so it is **not** constructed to always pass. But N1 itself is a sanity check, not a strong control — do not overstate its evidential weight.
- **Is any address a guess dressed as derivation?** The Func offset is honestly flagged as unmeasured. The residual risk is G6 (leg-1 static table). The verified-address discipline is otherwise good: target UFunction by reflection, ProcessEvent by proven slot 77, entry-point from the PE header, `.text` range from section headers via live base.
- **Does it honor every owner constraint verbatim?** Mostly, with two frictions: G5 (phase-2 adds an unauthorized second call) and G8 (the "nothing persistent" overstatement vs. the deliberate permanent leak).

Net: the mechanism's core is source-accurate and the exactly-once/restore-first logic is sound. The design's real weaknesses are (1) it never surveyed the zero-engine-write families that may be narrower than its own recommendation (G1), (2) it couples a low-risk phase-1 proof to a higher-risk phase-2 carrier by choice (G2/G3), and (3) it carries one wrong supporting rationale (G7 float-parm) and one unverified static-table dependency (G6) into otherwise careful gating.

### The non-POD problem, and why it is solvable

The **only** non-POD member in the whole 48-byte buffer is `SubPathString` (`FString`) at `Parms+0x18`.

**An empty `FString` IS safely representable as zeroed memory.** `FString` is exactly a `TArray<TCHAR, TSizedDefaultAllocator<32>>` (`UnrealString.h.inl:51-57`), i.e. `{Data=nullptr, ArrayNum=0, ArrayMax=0}`. The heap allocator's destructor is `FORCEINLINE ~ForAnyElementType() { if(Data) { … FMemory::Free(Data); } }` (`ContainerAllocationPolicies.h:471-481`) — null-guarded. `FString::Len()` returns `Data.Num() ? Data.Num()-1 : 0` (`UnrealString.h.inl:1082-1085`) → 0. So a zeroed 16 bytes is a valid, destructible, empty `FString`. **Zero-filling the Parms buffer is therefore not just hygiene, it is what makes the FString legal.** Likewise `FWeakObjectPtr{0,0}`: `Internal_GetObjectItem()` returns `nullptr` immediately when `ObjectSerialNumber == 0` (`WeakObjectPtr.h:265-278`), and the only thing distinguishing the two `#if UE_WEAKOBJECTPTR_ZEROINIT_FIX` branches there is a `checkSlow`, compiled out in Shipping. Zeroed weak-ptr is safe **either way the macro resolves** — which removes that uncertainty entirely, and is also what forces `LoadSynchronous` down the resolve/load path (`SoftObjectPtr.h:52-63`: `Get()` returns null → `ToSoftObjectPath().TryLoad()`).

Can `SubPathString` stay empty for our target? **Yes, guaranteed by the parser.** `FSoftObjectPath::SetPath(FWideStringView)` splits on `FAsciiSet(".") + SUBOBJECT_DELIMITER_CHAR` and takes the branch `SoftObjectPath.cpp:147-154`:
```
FWideStringView AssetNameView = FAsciiSet::FindPrefixWithout(Path, Delimiters);
if (AssetNameView.Len() == Path.Len())
{
    // No subobject path
    AssetPath = FTopLevelAssetPath(FName(PackageNameView), FName(AssetNameView));
    SubPathString.Empty();
    return;
}
```
`/Game/ModKit/MK_Canary.MK_Canary` has one `.` and no `:`, so it lands here and `SubPathString` is left empty. If we ever needed a *non-empty* `SubPathString`, that would be a genuine blocker (we'd be handed an engine-`FMemory::Malloc`'d buffer we cannot free from MinGW) — so **hard-constrain the target path to contain no `:`**.

### Can the FNames be supplied as raw `(ComparisonIndex, Number)` pairs? — Yes *mechanically*, but see §3

Structurally, yes: `FName` is two `uint32`s and nothing else in this build, so writing a `(ComparisonIndex, Number)` pair harvested from the live `FNamePool` via ERI I-03 produces a bit-identical `FName` to one the engine would construct. `Number` is stored as **actual+1** ("stored internally as 1 more than actual, so zero'd memory will be the default, no-instance case", `NameTypes.h:1110-1111`), so a plain unnumbered name harvested from the pool must be written with `Number = 0`. That is a real trap for anyone tempted to write `Number = 1`.

The catch is not the encoding. It is §3.

## 3. The FNames we need do not exist in the game — this IS a real obstacle, and it has a clean way around it

**The finding.** Exact-match counts against `research/evidence/RF-01/global-names.txt` (OBSERVED):

| name | present |
|---|---|
| `MK_Canary` | **0** |
| `ModKit` | **0** |
| `CT05Row` | **0** |
| `CT05CANARY8F4A2E1C` | **0** |
| `CT05MIRROR` | **0** |
| `MirrorEntryType` | **0** |
| `MirroredName` | **0** |
| `MirrorTableRow` | 1 |
| `DataTable` | 1 |
| `SoftObjectPath` | 1 |

(`MirrorTableRow` and `DataTable` are present because the RowStruct is the *engine's* `FMirrorTableRow` — `MirrorDataTable.h:43 struct FMirrorTableRow : public FTableRowBase` — and appears at `script-objects.tsv:12570 … /Script/Engine/MirrorTableRow`, with `/Script/Engine/DataTable` at line 7796. Only the names *we* authored are missing. That is exactly the expected pattern and it validates the check.)

**Why it bites.** `FSoftObjectPath` stores the package path as a *single* `FName` covering the whole `/Game/ModKit/MK_Canary` string. There is no way to compose it from existing name entries. A "find-only" `FName` lookup for a string not in the pool yields `NAME_None` — and `FSoftObjectPath::IsNull()` is `AssetPath.IsNull()` is `PackageName.IsNone()` (`SoftObjectPath.h:236-239`, `TopLevelAssetPath.h:110-113`). `LoadSynchronous` would then early-out at `if (Asset == nullptr && !IsNull())` (`SoftObjectPtr.h:55`) and return `nullptr` **silently**, with no exception and no log — the worst possible failure mode: it looks like "the game refused to load our package" when in fact we never asked. **This alone would have produced a false negative for ESC-02.**

**Why hand-writing pool entries is not the answer.** Inserting into `FNamePool` from a `CreateRemoteThread` thread means replicating `FNamePool`'s shard/lock/block-allocation protocol by hand against a live allocator. That is far outside the "narrowest and most verifiable" bar and I do not recommend it.

**The way around it: let the engine create the FNames, via reflection, with a string.** Both required entry points exist in *this* game's reflection data (OBSERVED):

```
script-objects.tsv:11836  5fbf4db1648bbd9b  57828571c49eba95  …  /Script/Engine/KismetSystemLibrary/MakeSoftObjectPath
script-objects.tsv:11663  5dbc3ae2795c68f9  57828571c49eba95  …  /Script/Engine/KismetSystemLibrary/Conv_SoftObjPathToSoftObjRef
script-objects.tsv:11571  4b235206248c780f  54d096799ec6d5fe  …  /Script/Engine/KismetStringLibrary/Conv_StringToName
```
```
KismetSystemLibrary.h:289-291
	/** Builds a Soft Object Path struct from a string that contains a full /folder/packagename.object path */
	UFUNCTION(BlueprintPure, Category = "Utilities", meta = (Keywords = "construct build", NativeMakeFunc, BlueprintThreadSafe, BlueprintAutocast))
	static ENGINE_API FSoftObjectPath MakeSoftObjectPath(const FString& PathString);

KismetSystemLibrary.cpp:1273-1284  → FSoftObjectPath SoftObjectPath(PathString);  (+ a LogRuntimeError if !IsValid)
```
`FSoftObjectPath(const FString&)` (`SoftObjectPath.h:51`) → `SetPath(FStringView)` → `FName(PackageNameView)` / `FName(AssetNameView)`, which are **find-or-add** constructors. The engine inserts both names into the live pool itself, on the GameThread, using its own code. That is the whole problem, solved.

**Predicted Parms for `MakeSoftObjectPath` (INFERRED; verify ParmsSize/ReturnValueOffset live the same way):**
```
+0x00  PathString  : FStrProperty, 16 bytes   { TCHAR* Data ; int32 Num ; int32 Max }
+0x10  ReturnValue : FStructProperty(FSoftObjectPath), 32 bytes
+0x30  == ParmsSize ;  ReturnValueOffset = 0x10
```

**Ownership analysis for the input FString (this is the load-bearing part):** we supply `{Data = <our own buffer>, ArrayNum = Len+1, ArrayMax = Len+1}` with a UTF-16LE, **null-terminated** string (`ArrayNum` must include the terminator — `FString::Len()` is `Num-1`, `UnrealString.h.inl:1082-1085`).
- `ProcessEvent` does `FMemory::Memcpy(Frame, Parms, Function->ParmsSize)` (`ScriptCore.cpp:2078-2081`) — a *bitwise* copy; nothing is constructed.
- The thunk's `P_GET_PROPERTY_REF` path goes through `FFrame::StepCompiledInRef` (`Stack.h:524-543`) → `StepExplicitProperty` (`ScriptCore.cpp:481-505`), which for a non-out param does `CopyCompleteValueToScriptVM_InContainer(Result, Locals)`. That is an `FString` **copy-assign into an engine-allocated temporary** — it *reads* our buffer and mallocs its own. The temporary is destroyed by the thunk.
- On exit, `ScriptCore.cpp:2145-2157`: for a `DestructorLink` property that *is* inside the parms region and is not `CPF_OutParm`, ProcessEvent **memcpy's the frame copy back over `Parms`** rather than destroying it — "so the correct copy is destroyed when the event function returns". Bits identical to what we wrote.

Net: **the engine never calls `FMemory::Free` on our buffer.** We own it (a static array inside the probe DLL is fine) and we simply never hand it to the engine's allocator. This is the one safe way to cross the MinGW↔MSVC boundary with an `FString`, and it works *only* because the parameter is an input.

**Ownership analysis for the returned `FSoftObjectPath`:** ProcessEvent computes `ReturnValueAddress = (uint8*)Parms + Function->ReturnValueOffset` (`ScriptCore.cpp:2138-2141`) — the thunk assigns **directly into our buffer**. `FSoftObjectPath::operator=` runs `FString` copy-assign with our zeroed 16 bytes as the destination, which is legal (empty, null-guarded). And per `SoftObjectPath.cpp:147-154` above, the resulting `SubPathString` is **empty** for our delimiter-free path, so **no engine-allocated memory lands in our buffer.** Confirm this by asserting `Parms[0x10+0x10 .. 0x10+0x1F] == 0` after the call. If it is ever non-zero, **stop** — we would be holding an engine allocation we cannot free.

### Concrete byte-level plan (one GameThread callback, two ProcessEvent calls)

All three UObject addresses come from ERI's proven NAME→ADDRESS oracle (I-04/I-05); no raw RVA anywhere except the already-proven `ProcessEvent` vtable slot 77.

```
PRE-FLIGHT (read-only, ERI, before any escalation)
  resolve /Script/Engine.KismetSystemLibrary, :MakeSoftObjectPath, :LoadAsset_Blocking,
          /Script/Engine.Default__KismetSystemLibrary
  assert MakeSoftObjectPath  : NumParms==2, ParmsSize==0x30, ReturnValueOffset==0x10
  assert LoadAsset_Blocking  : NumParms==2, ParmsSize==0x30, ReturnValueOffset==0x28
  assert /Script/CoreUObject.SoftObjectPath UScriptStruct PropertiesSize==32   (offset +0x58, INFERRED)
  ANY mismatch  ->  abort, do not escalate.

STEP A  (inside the one GameThread callback)
  static const wchar_t PATH[] = L"/Game/ModKit/MK_Canary.MK_Canary";   // 32 chars + NUL, no ':'
  uint8 A[0x30]; memset(A, 0, 0x30);
  *(void**)(A+0x00) = (void*)PATH;
  *(int32*)(A+0x08) = 33;      // Len+1, MUST include terminator
  *(int32*)(A+0x0C) = 33;
  ProcessEvent(Default__KismetSystemLibrary, MakeSoftObjectPath, A);   // vtable slot 77
  // A+0x10 .. A+0x2F now holds a fully-formed FSoftObjectPath
  assert *(uint32*)(A+0x10) != 0;                  // PackageName.ComparisonIndex non-zero == not NAME_None
  assert bytes A+0x20 .. A+0x2F are all zero;      // SubPathString empty -> nothing to free

STEP B  (same callback)
  uint8 B[0x30]; memset(B, 0, 0x30);
  memcpy(B+0x08, A+0x10, 32);                      // FSoftObjectPath into TSoftObjectPtr::ObjectID
                                                   // B+0x00..0x07 stays zero == null FWeakObjectPtr
  ProcessEvent(Default__KismetSystemLibrary, LoadAsset_Blocking, B);
  UObject* Result = *(UObject**)(B+0x28);

VERIFY (read-only, ERI, after)
  Result != nullptr; its NamePrivate decodes to "MK_Canary";
  its ClassPrivate is /Script/Engine.DataTable;
  /Game/ModKit/MK_Canary now exists as a UPackage in GUObjectArray;
  the FNames "/Game/ModKit/MK_Canary" and "MK_Canary" are now in the live FNamePool
      (they were not before — that transition is itself independent proof the call ran).
  Leak accounting: exactly zero engine allocations retained by us.
```

Nothing here constructs a C++ object in MinGW-compiled code. Every non-POD value is either all-zero bytes (provably a valid empty `FString` / null `FWeakObjectPtr`) or produced by MSVC-compiled engine code writing into our buffer.

Two side effects to declare up front, both benign and both irreversible-but-harmless: the live `FNamePool` permanently gains two entries (`FNamePool` never shrinks anyway, and any normal load would do the same), and `MakeSoftObjectPath` calls `LogRuntimeError` if the path fails to parse (`KismetSystemLibrary.cpp:1276-1281`) — the format string is stripped in this build, so expect no visible output, which is why the `ComparisonIndex != 0` assertion carries the check instead.

The obvious narrow one-shot is to swap `UFunction::Func` on a per-frame UFunction, let it fire once, and restore it. **We cannot currently compute that field's offset.** `eri.py:4800-4808` says so explicitly and deliberately refuses to read it:

> "RPCId/RPCResponseId (+0xBA/+0xBC) and everything after — including every `#if UE_BLUEPRINT_EVENTGRAPH_FASTCALLS` / `#if WITH_LIVE_CODING` conditionally-compiled field and the native Func pointer — are DELIBERATELY never read (real, unresolved conditional-compilation uncertainty this pass does not attempt to resolve)"

From source the defaults are `UE_BLUEPRINT_EVENTGRAPH_FASTCALLS 1` (`Build.h:363-365`) and `WITH_LIVE_CODING 0` (`Build.h:153-155`), which with the `Class.h:1797-1830` declaration order gives (**INFERRED, NOT VERIFIED**):
```
+0xB0 FunctionFlags   +0xB4 NumParms   +0xB5 pad   +0xB6 ParmsSize   +0xB8 ReturnValueOffset
+0xBA RPCId           +0xBC RPCResponseId          +0xBE pad(2)
+0xC0 FirstPropertyToInit   +0xC8 EventGraphFunction   +0xD0 EventGraphCallOffset   +0xD4 pad(4)
+0xD8 Func            sizeof(UFunction) = 0xE0
```
Both are `#ifndef` guards that UBT can override, and this build's `.pdata` gives us no names to check against. **Do not write to `+0xD8` on this claim.** It is verifiable cheaply and read-only first: for a *native* UFunction (e.g. `/Script/MISERY.MiseryBlueprintFunctionLibrary:IsSteamDeck`, already proven callable) read the 8 bytes at `+0xD8` and confirm they land inside the module's `.text` **and** on a `.pdata` RUNTIME_FUNCTION *start* boundary; then confirm that many distinct Blueprint-implemented UFunctions (which all route to `UObject::ProcessInternal`) share one identical value at `+0xD8` while native ones do not. Two independent structural signals, zero writes. Only after that does a Func-swap become a defensible escalation.

`UFunction::Invoke` is `return (*Func)(Obj, Stack, RESULT_PARAM);` (`Class.cpp:6836-6848`), so a swap there is genuinely narrow — one pointer, restored inside the same call. But it is not yet earned.

Two further design notes for the hook target, from source:
- `AActor::Tick` reaches `ReceiveTick` only under `if (GetClass()->HasAnyClassFlags(CLASS_CompiledFromBlueprint) || !GetClass()->HasAnyClassFlags(CLASS_Native))` and `GetWorldSettings() != nullptr` (`Actor.cpp:1495-1504`). Native-only actors never call it. BP actors do.
- `ProcessEvent`'s very first statement is `checkf(!IsUnreachable(), … "Alternatively, this function was called from a non-GameThread which is unsafe.")` (`ScriptCore.cpp:1974-1976`) — compiled out in Shipping, which is precisely why the off-thread ESC-01 call did not trip anything. That is a reason to be *more* careful, not less: the engine's own guardrail against exactly what we are doing is absent from this build.

- §1 is confirmed statically and cleanly; close the live gap with one ERI by-name read before escalating.
- §2 has a complete, buildable 48-byte plan with exactly one non-POD field, and that field is provably safe as zeroed memory.
- §3 was a real, silent-failure-shaped obstacle — the FNames genuinely are absent — and `MakeSoftObjectPath` (present at `script-objects.tsv:11836`) dissolves it by making the engine mint the names itself from a string whose buffer we own and the engine never frees.
- §4 gives concrete live targets, but the `UFunction::Func` offset is **not** established in this project and must not be written to on inference alone.
